NOT REFUTED. I attacked each clause-(i) model of SM.turnlift (work/reviews/cf-lem-turnlift-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt) against sm-3:3542-3552 and its proof 3579-3619 and could not produce an instance the printed lemma covers but the Lean excludes (or the reverse) with a different or vacuous conclusion.

1. Reparam (stmt lines 116-120; field tw_reparam 562). Printed class (3549, proof 3598-3601): an orientation-preserving reparametrisation of the circle R/Z, "with an increasing representative phi: R -> R, phi(s+1) = phi(s)+1". An orientation-preserving homeomorphism of R/Z lifts to a continuous strictly increasing phi with phi(s+1)=phi(s)+1 (degree +1), and conversely every such phi is a homeomorphism of R (continuity + add_one give surjectivity; I proved Reparam.surjective in a scratch file) and descends to an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of R/Z; all lifts differ by integers, so T∘phi is the same loop. Hence Reparam = printed class exactly. Reparametrisations not fixing 0 are included (phi(0) is free; Reparam.shift a := s+a compiles), so seam independence is a special case, as printed ("every interval of length one has the same increment", 3597-3598). Candidate attacks fail: (a) strictly increasing but discontinuous degree-one maps (e.g. phi = s/2 on [0,1/2), s/2+1/2 on [1/2,1), extended by add_one) are rightly excluded: they are not homeomorphisms and T∘phi need not be continuous, so the printed conclusion is not even posed. (b) weakly monotone degree-one continuous maps are not "reparametrisations" (not bijective); and even for them theta∘phi lifts T∘phi with the same increment, so admitting them would not change the conclusion. StrictMono is unused by the proof (plan line 41) — a non-blocking "stronger hypothesis than the argument needs", but it is exactly the printed class. (c) degree-k covers (s -> ks) would change tw by k and are correctly excluded by add_one.

2. DirectionHomotopy (stmt lines 152-156; field tw_homotopy 564). Printed (3549-3550, proof 3603-3616): a continuous homotopy T(s,t) through direction loops; the proof uses uniform continuity in (s,t), i.e. joint continuity, and periodicity T(1,t)=T(0,t). Lean: H : R x R -> Plane jointly continuous (Continuous on the product), each H(t,.) 1-periodic and unit. The only difference is t in R vs [0,1]; it is content-neutral: for a printed H0 : Icc 0 1 x R -> Plane, H(t,s) := H0(projIcc 0 1 t, s) is a DirectionHomotopy whose loop t equals H0(t,.) for t in [0,1] (I compiled DirectionHomotopy.ofIcc and ofIcc_H_of_mem against SM.TurningNumber, exit 0), so the Lean field yields tw(T(.,0)) = tw(T(.,1)); conversely any Lean instance restricted to [t,t'] and rescaled is a printed homotopy. By the exponential law (R/Z compact) joint continuity is also equivalent to continuity into the loop space with the uniform topology, so no weaker standard reading is missed.

3. RegularHomotopy (stmt lines 191-198; field rot_regular_homotopy 567). The source never defines "regular homotopy" (grep over reference/: only uses at sm-3:3551, 3616, CV d1_setup 796/860, d6 1472/1624/1791, d10 576). The printed proof fixes the intended class: "A regular homotopy supplies such a homotopy of normalised tangents" (3616-3617), i.e. (t,s) -> gamma_t'(s)/|gamma_t'(s)| is a continuous homotopy through direction loops, which requires the s-derivative to be jointly continuous and nonvanishing. That is exactly Lean's hasDerivAt + continuous_deriv + regular + periodic (+ Continuous Gamma, part of any "homotopy"). By the exponential law this equals a continuous path in the C^1 topology on immersions S^1 -> R^2 (the Whitney-Graustein notion). Attacks: (a) the weaker reading "C^0 homotopy through regular curves" is not a faithful alternative because under it the printed claim is false: a circle with a tangential curl of size eps -> 0 (rotation 2, every stage C^1 regular) converges uniformly to the circle (rotation 1), a jointly continuous family of regular curves whose rotation jumps; only derivative continuity in t excludes it, and the printed proof relies on exactly that. (b) stricter readings (C^1 or smooth in (t,s)) are Lean instances, since Lean asks no t-differentiability, so the Lean theorem is at least as strong. (c) t in R vs [0,1]: RegularHomotopy.ofIcc via projIcc compiles (HasDerivAt is per fixed t, so projIcc composition is harmless), and curve 0 / curve 1 are the printed ends up to proof-irrelevant fields.

4. ClosedC1Curve.reverse (stmt lines 237-249; field rot_reverse 569). Printed oppositely oriented curve: -T_gamma(1-s) with lift theta(1-s)+pi (3617-3619), i.e. s -> gamma(1-s). Lean uses gamma(-s); by 1-periodicity gamma(-s) = gamma(1-s) and -gamma'(-s) = -gamma'(1-s) (deriv_periodic), so the two are the same function with the same derivative.
